summary: Concurrent region rollouts overload coordinator queue and delay pin handshake, causing silent fallback to compat variant
description: Customer (Acme Payments) reported intermittent quality regressions starting 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC: some requests pinned to their explicitly requested gptx-3.2-quantized model were being served by the compat variant (gptx-3.2-compat) without a visible error, producing lower-quality responses and increased token usage. This occurred during a scheduled multi-region canary rollout we had started earlier that morning.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer pins requests to gptx-3.2-quantized via model param and uses low-latency route in us-east.
2) Start a concurrent canary rollout in us-east and eu-west that updates model variants and prewarm tasks.
3) Observe that a subset (~4-6%) of pinned requests are silently routed to compatibility variant.
4) Replay logs from affected request IDs and correlate with orchestrator rollout queue length at that timestamp.
logs:
2026-03-10T02:40:12.123Z edge-proxy[ingress] request_id=acme-xx pin_token=abc123 target_model=gptx-3.2-quantized routed_model=gptx-3.2-compat
2026-03-10T02:40:12.126Z orchestrator[coordinator] WARN queue_length=312 priority_inversion_detected=false task=health_probe id=hp-992
2026-03-10T02:40:12.129Z orchestrator[coordinator] INFO handshake_start request_id=acme-xx pin_state=awaiting_commit
2026-03-10T02:40:12.231Z orchestrator[coordinator] ERROR handshake_timeout request_id=acme-xx reason=coordination-starvation
2026-03-10T02:40:12.232Z router[route-decider] INFO fallback_to_variant request_id=acme-xx fallback_model=gptx-3.2-compat reason=pin_handshake_timeout
(See attached debug trace: /var/log/redwood/debug/acme/2026-03-10.trace)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: prewarm or health probe work flooded the coordinator queue and delayed the pin commit handshake.
- Observed coordinator queue spikes correlated with simultaneous canary prewarm tasks across regions.
- The new scheduler change (PR 1987) introduced a single shared priority queue for control-plane tasks; low-cost probes were not being deprioritized correctly, causing priority inversion under load.
- Edge trace shows handshake timeout (120ms threshold) being exceeded while coordinator processed probe tasks.
- Reproduced locally by replaying canary prewarm workload: when coordinator queue >250 tasks, handshake success rate drops to ~92% and fallback rate increases accordingly.
- No errors in auth or model catalog: the router correctly selected fallback after handshake failure (intended behavior), but customer expectation was strict pin retention.
- Billing spike explained by compat variant producing larger token counts in this model pair (quantized outputs truncated differently).
customer_impact: Acme Payments reported degraded user experience for ~4% of their requests during rollout window; several QA alerts and 3 merchant-reported incidents of failed validation due to lower-quality completions. No data leakage observed. Incident caused measurable latency increase for affected sessions and a small billing delta (estimated +6% for that hour).
workaround:
1) Temporarily pause concurrent cross-region canary rollouts for this customer.
2) Add explicit rollout exclusion tag for enterprise customers with pinned sessions (applied to Acme Payments) to prevent prewarm flooding on their control-plane shards.
3) Increase pin handshake timeout to 500ms for the customer's route as a short-term mitigation.
resolution:
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-11 09:30 UTC: reverted the priority queue change in PR 1987 and introduced a priority-aware queueing patch (PR 1999) that deprioritizes probe/prewarm tasks during coordinator load spikes.
- Coordinator handshake timeout default revised from 120ms -> 250ms cluster-wide; customer-specific handshake timeout set to 500ms during rollback window.
- Re-ran customer replay and verified pinned requests remained on gptx-3.2-quantized.
- Notified Acme Payments and issued credit for the billing delta.
Follow-up: full postmortem scheduled, and new canary rules will prevent concurrent multi-region prewarm waves for routes tagged as 'enterprise-pinned'.
